question: Can equal-mass static-compliance and regenerative-stability rankings disagree in a clamped thin strip? This known distinction is a solver check, not claimed novelty.

hypotheses.H0: The static-compliance optimum is also best in the chosen sampled stability objective.
hypotheses.H1: A different equal-mass profile has a larger sampled stability objective; any benefit may depend on speed, contact point, damping and modeling approximation.

parameter_provenance: All geometry, material, damping and cutting numbers are declared illustrative scenario assumptions, not measured or calibrated parameters of the user's part.
selection: Grid-search static tip compliance and the minimum averaged-DDE boundary over all screening contacts and speeds. Also retain the best mean-boundary profile. No algorithm training.

project_gates.numerical: Uniform beam first-mode error <0.1%, static compliance error <0.01%; selected boundaries change <5% at finest step refinements, or mark unresolved.
project_gates.signal: For a future research decision require >=10% robust objective benefit beyond numerical error and a genuine advance over closest literature. These are project gates, not publication thresholds.
project_gates.stop: No ranking difference, loss under periodic verification, sensitivity to arbitrary damping, or no substantive literature gap: do not launch a large optimizer or neural network. Preserve null/negative results.

budget: Bounded CPU pilot only; no GPU training, software install, production changes, or unattended long experiments.
independence: All grid points are deterministic scenario evaluations, not independent experimental samples. Averaged vs periodic and frequency vs RK4 comparisons are model/numerical checks, not real-world validation.
